Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: SOC 2 revalidation + retention change for renewal (HarborPay)

Hi Marissa,

We're starting our renewal checklist for Redwood (contract expires 2026-12-31) and have a couple of compliance asks before we sign the amendment:

- HarborPay needs confirmation of your SOC 2 re-attestation timeline (are you scheduling the audit for Q1 2027?).
- We need a mapped evidence inventory we can hand to our internal auditors (ideally a simple CSV with artifact names, owner, and delivery window).
- We're evaluating a 2-year retention window for audit logs instead of 1 year — can Redwood support an exception on our account? If so, what's the impact on cost and export mechanics?

Separately, product wants to increase concurrent seat/throughput for a pilot (approx +30% at renewal). Please include any pricing guidance and how a seat/top-up shows up on the dedicated capacity plan.

Can you put together a short mutual action plan and timeline by next week? Procurement will need terms for DocuSign and a statement of evidence availability for their auditors.

Thanks,
Sophie
Sophie Tran
Head of Security Operations | HarborPay

Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SOC 2 revalidation + retention change for renewal (HarborPay)

Sophie — thanks for the clear list. High level answers below and I'll follow up with a one-page MAP and uploadable inventory by Friday.

Quick answers:
- Redwood is scheduling our SOC 2 Type II engagement for late Jan 2027 with the auditor (firm: Northbridge Assurance). We expect an attestation available by mid-March, with a draft control mapping usable for customer reviews in early Feb.
- We will provide an artifacts CSV (owner, path, retention policy, expected delivery date). I'll attach the checklist and a sample retention matrix.
- We can accommodate a 2-year audit-log retention carve-out for HarborPay. There is a configuration and modest storage uplift; operationally we expose an export endpoint for raw logs (S3 presigned) and maintain a separate retention tag for audit queries. I'll include estimated incremental costs in the MAP.

Upsell/Capacity:
- Seat/throughput increases for Dedicated: we can offer a pro-rated seat top-up effective on the amendment date; a 30% uplift looks like a small dedicated pool increase — I'll run numbers with Ben and return a pricing option: 1) committed monthly uplift (lower unit), 2) burst bucket (on-demand at higher unit cost).

Next steps
- I'll drop the mutual-action-plan, the evidence checklist, and retention matrix to this thread by EOD Friday (2026-11-20).
- Ben will model the cost options for the seat increase and provide comparative unit economics.
- Kimberly will coordinate the DocuSign/contract amendment language and the clause for retention carve-outs.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SOC 2 revalidation + retention change for renewal (HarborPay)

Hi Sophie — Ben here (solutions and pricing). I ran the capacity numbers this morning. Short summary:

1) Pricing impacts for 2-year retention (audit logs): estimated additional monthly cost ~$1,250 for the extra storage and export indexing (this is a rough estimate; I'll provide a line-item breakdown in the MAP).

2) Seat/throughput uplift options (for 30% demand bump):
   - Option A (Committed uplift): +30% reserved throughput on current Dedicated pool — adds $4,500/mo (discounted if you sign a 12-month commit).
   - Option B (Burst bucket): on-demand burst credits — pay-per-use, no commit, expected ~25% higher unit cost but zero upfront.

3) Operational notes: the retention-carveout will be configured at account-level and we will tag the HarborPay logs with "retention:24m" for policy enforcement. Exports will be available from the admin console and via an S3 presign link that Redwood Support can generate for your auditors.

I attached a quick table (CSV) showing storage math for 12/24 month windows with sample monthly deltas.

If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-minute call Thursday to walk the team through the MAP and cost options; otherwise I will post the finalized MAP and cost table by EOD Friday.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

Marissa — appreciate the quick turnaround.

Couple clarifying asks before we finalize the MAP: 
- For the retention carve-out, will Redwood maintain separate audit indices so we can run queries without affecting production telemetry? We need assurance that queries won't impact latency SLAs.
- For the export proof-of-delivery, can you include a sample presigned URL flow and an estimated time-to-delivery SLA (we'd like exports within 48 hours of request during the audit period).
- Finally, procurement wants the DocuSign draft in parallel so legal can review the amended retention clause. Could Kimberly share a redline with the 2-year retention clause and the committed seat option?

If those items look good, we can lock the amendment and route DocuSign by Nov 30. I'll also loop in our internal auditors if they need to review the artifacts directly.

Regards,
Sophie

Sophie — Kimberly here on legal & contracts. Attached is a draft amendment with the 2-year retention clause and two commercial appendices (Committed Uplift, Burst Credits). Key callouts:

- Retention Clause: we will amend Section 4.2 to include a customer-specific retention override. The clause spells out data segregation, retention tag usage, and export mechanics.
- SLA for exports: Redwood will provide a best-effort export within 48 hours; for guaranteed 48-hour SLA we can include an incidentable clause with a small fee — I noted both flavors in Appendix B.
- Pricing: Committed uplift pricing includes a 10% discount on the uplift line if you sign a 12-month extension at the new committed level.

I'll also include a short operational runbook for auditors (how to request exports, who to contact, redwood support playbook). If the amendment text looks good, I'll open a DocuSign envelope and cc your procurement mailbox.
